region: Europe and West Asia (Istanbul and Anatolia, Ottoman Empire)
title: The Turkish People: Their Social Life, Religious Beliefs and Institutions, and Domestic Life
author: Lucy M. J. Garnett
notes: London: Methuen. Opened full text: complete through conclusion, glossary and index (a Methuen catalogue of about 20k words follows and is excluded from the count). OCR clean. Part I social life (capital, officials, palace, provincial and country folk, holidays); Part II religious beliefs and institutions; Part III domestic life (harem system, birth and circumcision, marriage, funeral ceremonies, home life). Descriptive survey by a long-time resident, not a travel narrative. Same author's Turkish Life in Town and Country (1904, IA turkishlifeintow00garnrich) covers the same society (not opened).

title: The Sia
author: Matilda Coxe Stevenson
notes: Offprint of 11th Annual Report of the Bureau of Ethnology (1889-90), pp. 3-157 (raw OCR count 75.7k incl. plate captions and noise). Contents: cosmogony, cult societies, rain and healing ceremonials, songs, childbirth, mortuary customs and beliefs, myths. Mainly religion and ritual; little on kinship or law. Complete except that OCR drops the final word ('victim.') of the last page; the full-volume scan sia00stevgoog has it. OCR readable with scattered errors.

region: North America (Southeast; Alabama, Georgia, later Oklahoma)
title: Social Organization and Social Usages of the Indians of the Creek Confederacy
author: John R. Swanton
notes: In 42nd Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology (1924-25), printed Washington 1928 (title page checked); the paper is pp. 23-472 (about 174k words). Companion paper in the same volume, pp. 473-672: Religious Beliefs and Medical Practices of the Creek Indians (about 96k words). The volume also holds unrelated papers; use those page ranges. Covers clans, towns, government, law, kinship, marriage, life cycle. Confederacy towns included some non-Muskogee speakers (Hitchiti, Alabama, Koasati, Yuchi); Yuchi already in candidates.csv, so restrict to Creek proper if needed. OCR clean. Alternate scan: annualreportofbu42smithso.

region: North America (Southeast; northern Mississippi, later Oklahoma)
title: Social and Religious Beliefs and Usages of the Chickasaw Indians
author: John R. Swanton
notes: In 44th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology (1926-27), printed Washington 1928 (title page checked); the paper is pp. 169-273 (about 53k words). Origin legends, kinship terms, personal names, social organization, government, property, crime and punishment, women, childbirth and education, marriage, death, religion. Volume holds other papers (Burton Mound, Chippewa plants, archaeology). OCR clean. Alternate scan: annualreportofbu44smithso.

title: Japan: An Attempt at Interpretation
author: Lafcadio Hearn
notes: Complete Project Gutenberg text with index. Interpretive monograph on Japanese religion and society: the ancient cult, religion of the home, the Japanese family, the communal cult, Shinto, worship and purification, rule of the dead, Buddhism, social organization; later chapters (rise of military power, feudal integration, persecution of Christianity, modern restraints, education) are historical. Not a travel narrative, but historically framed. More ethnographic alternative for the same society (opened, complete, about 96k words): Alice Mabel Bacon, Japanese Girls and Women (1891, rev. 1902), https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/32449/pg32449.txt (women's life cycle, marriage, domestic life, peasant and samurai women).

other_names: Haidah; Masset Haida; Haida of the Queen Charlotte Islands (Haida Gwaii)
title: Ancient Warriors of the North Pacific: The Haidas, Their Laws, Customs and Legends, with Some Historical Account of the Queen Charlotte Islands
author: Charles Harrison
notes: London: H. F. & G. Witherby, 1925 (title page checked). Author was a missionary at Masset ('forty years residence amongst the Haidas'). Chapters III-XII (about 70% of text) on the Haida: clans, chieftaincy and potlatch, laws and customs, birth, marriage, divorce, death and burial, masks, industries, shaman, pantheon, legends; chapters I-II and XIII-XIV are geography, early history, natural history, geology. Complete with index; OCR good after the noisy cover pages. Open-access item (collection internetarchivebooks, not lending-restricted). Swanton's Contributions to the Ethnology of the Haida (1905) is not on IA or PG.

title: The Cayapa Indians of Ecuador
author: S. A. Barrett
notes: Museum of the American Indian, Heye Foundation, Indian Notes and Monographs No. 40, two parts (multi-volume). Part 1 (about 51k words): https://archive.org/stream/cayapaindiansofe01barr/cayapaindiansofe01barr_djvu.txt ; Part 2 (about 69k words): https://archive.org/stream/cayapaindiansofe02barr/cayapaindiansofe02barr_djvu.txt . Both opened, complete (part 2 has index), OCR clean. Part 1: territory, resources, history, daily life, material culture; Part 2: textiles, decorative art, then government, birth, names, puberty, marriage, death, kinship terms, medicine and shamanism, religion, mythology, ceremonial fiestas, physical anthropology. Social-life sections are roughly 25-30k words; most of the work is material culture.

title: The Ethnology of the Salinan Indians
author: J. Alden Mason
notes: University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology vol. 10 no. 4, pp. 97-240 (text to p. 205, then plates); the IA item is the whole bound vol. 10 with other papers, so use that page range. Contents: geography, history (pre-mission, mission, post-mission), economic life, material culture, art, music, social life (birth, puberty, marriage, sickness, death, kinship terms, government, games, dances, trade, warfare), religion, shamanism, mythology. Salvage ethnography from mission records and a few informants; social life and religion are about a third. Only modestly above the 30k-word threshold. OCR clean.

title: The Sacred Formulas of the Cherokees
author: James Mooney
notes: WEAK candidate. 7th Annual Report of the Bureau of Ethnology (1885-86, printed 1891), pp. 301-397; complete PG transcription. Covers religion and medicine only (Cherokee theory of disease, shamans, medical practice, taboo, sweat bath, medicine dances, gods, color symbolism, names) plus about half specimen formulas in Cherokee with translations and commentary; no kinship or law. Mooney's Myths of the Cherokee (1900, PG 45634) is longer but is mainly history and myths (not opened in full).
